record.object_value:
## Severity

- **Severity:** Low
- **CVSS v3.1:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N` (3.7, Low)
- **CWE:** CWE-440 (Expected Behavior Violation), CWE-668 (Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere)

## Summary

vLLM V1 `InputBatch.condense()` can leave a stale `allowed_token_ids_mask_cpu_tensor` row after moving a constrained request. A later unrestricted request that reuses that batch slot inherits the previous request's token allowlist, so sampling for that other client is constrained by a mask it did not set (cross-request output-integrity issue). The victim request still returns HTTP 200 with no error indication.

Public report: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43894

## Affected

- **Ecosystem / package:** pip / `vllm`
- **Affected versions:** vLLM ≤ 0.30.0 (V1 worker `InputBatch` path). Confirmed via public issue #43894.
- **Fixed versions:** Fix merged in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43931 (not yet in a tagged release as of v0.30.0; expected in the next release).

## Details

`InputBatch.condense()` copies `allowed_token_ids_mask_cpu_tensor` from a moved request's row into the freed index but never clears the source row. `add_request()` only writes that row when the new request sets `sampling_params.allowed_token_ids`. When another active request still has `allowed_token_ids`, `_make_sampling_metadata()` copies the active prefix of the CPU mask to GPU and `Sampler.apply_logits_processors()` applies the stale whitelist to the unrestricted request.

An attacker who can submit generate traffic (including unauthenticated `/invocations`, which is outside `--api-key` guards, or any valid API key on `/v1`) plants a chosen `allowed_token_ids` mask. /description: ## Severity

- **Severity:** Low
- **CVSS v3.1:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N` (3.7, Low)
- **CWE:** CWE-440 (Expected Behavior Violation), CWE-668 (Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere)

## Summary

vLLM V1 `InputBatch.condense()` can leave a stale `allowed_token_ids_mask_cpu_tensor` row after moving a constrained request. A later unrestricted request that reuses that batch slot inherits the previous request's token allowlist, so sampling for that other client is constrained by a mask it did not set (cross-request output-integrity issue). The victim request still returns HTTP 200 with no error indication.

Public report: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43894

## Affected

- **Ecosystem / package:** pip / `vllm`
- **Affected versions:** vLLM ≤ 0.30.0 (V1 worker `InputBatch` path). Confirmed via public issue #43894.
- **Fixed versions:** Fix merged in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43931 (not yet in a tagged release as of v0.30.0; expected in the next release).

## Details

`InputBatch.condense()` copies `allowed_token_ids_mask_cpu_tensor` from a moved request's row into the freed index but never clears the source row. `add_request()` only writes that row when the new request sets `sampling_params.allowed_token_ids`. When another active request still has `allowed_token_ids`, `_make_sampling_metadata()` copies the active prefix of the CPU mask to GPU and `Sampler.apply_logits_processors()` applies the stale whitelist to the unrestricted request.

An attacker who can submit generate traffic (including unauthenticated `/invocations`, which is outside `--api-key` guards, or any valid API key on `/v1`) plants a chosen `allowed_token_ids` mask. If batching/`condense` recycles that row onto another client's unrestricted request while the constrained request is still active, the victim's tokens are limited to the attacker's allowlist (for example only a single token, only digit tokens, or only tokens that spell a short phrase). This is vocabulary steering / wrong allowlist application, not free-form substitution of arbitrary attacker text.

A related but distinct bug in `InputBatch.swap_states()` (row-view aliasing of the same mask tensor) was fixed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48419.

## Impact

Limited cross-request sampling integrity on a shared engine: one client's `allowed_token_ids` can constrain another client's outputs under concurrent batching. Confidentiality and availability are unaffected. Attack complexity is High because exploitation needs concurrent requests plus a `condense` slot-reuse race while the attacker's constrained request remains in the batch.

## Patches

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43931 — clear vacated `allowed_token_ids` mask rows in `condense()`
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48419 — related `swap_states` mask aliasing fix

## References

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43894
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43931
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48419
- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/security.html (API key does not cover `/invocations`)

## Credit

Reported publicly by @glaziermag in issue #43894.
